related_questions.snippet: Updated Guidance: The updated Respiratory Virus Guidance recommends that people stay home and away from others until at least 24 hours after both their symptoms are getting better overall, and they have not had a fever (and are not using fever-reducing medication).

related_questions.question: Do you still have to isolate with COVID WA?
related_questions.snippet: There are currently no rules in WA that require you to self-isolate if you test positive for COVID-19. However, it is strongly recommended that you stay home for at least 5 days or until your symptoms have gone, and take steps to protect others.

related_questions.question: How many days must I isolate after testing positive for COVID?
related_questions.snippet: If you test positive, you are strongly encouraged to isolate (stay home and away from other people) for at least 5 full days, to prevent spreading the disease to others. Isolation is recommended even if you have been vaccinated or have had COVID-19 before.

related_questions.question: What to do immediately after being exposed to someone with COVID?
related_questions.title: Take Precautions Right Away
list: Start wearing a high-quality mask or respirator (such as N95) as soon as you find out you were exposed to someone with COVID-19.
You should wear a mask any time you are around others either inside your home or around other people in public.
Start counting from day 1 of exposure.
